nodes.label: Natural and Synthetic Polymers: Designing Rheological Properties
nodes.summary: Surveys rheological additives for aqueous systems (gums, cellulosics, starch derivatives, clays, PEGs, fatty alcohols, synthetic polymers) and nonaqueous systems (silicas, polyethylenes, fatty acids, castor oil derivatives, organoclays). Explains thixotropic vs pseudoplastic behavior, yield value, emulsion stabilization, suspension, foam, lubricity and conditioning functions and how to select additives.

nodes.label: Rheology Modifiers
nodes.summary: Ingredients that modify flow characteristics of a fluid and add functions such as suspension, emulsion stabilization, lubricity, and stability to shear, heat, pH and freeze/thaw.

nodes.label: Viscosity
nodes.summary: A measure of the resistance of a fluid to deformation or flow; higher viscosity contributes to emulsion stability and is associated with luxuriousness.

nodes.label: Thixotropy
nodes.summary: Shear thinning with delayed recovery: viscosity decreases under shear and recovers only over time after shear is removed.

nodes.label: Pseudoplasticity
nodes.summary: Shear thinning with immediate recovery when shear is removed; shown by xanthan and guar gums, carbomers, cellulosics, clays and silicas.

nodes.label: Yield Stress
nodes.summary: The stress required to initiate flow of a fluid; increasing yield value improves distribution and suspension stability of actives and particles.

nodes.label: Emulsion Stability
nodes.summary: Resistance of an emulsion to creaming, phase separation and coalescence; rheology modifiers in the external or internal phase slow droplet movement.

nodes.label: Syneresis
nodes.summary: Separation of water (or oil, 'sweating') from a gel or formulation; starch derivatives inhibit it in aqueous systems.

nodes.label: Emulsion
nodes.summary: A mixture of oil and water where one phase is suspended as tiny droplets in the other to create a stable dispersion.

nodes.label: Natural Gums
nodes.summary: Agricultural polysaccharide thickeners (carrageenan, xanthan, guar, tragacanth, locust bean, karaya, alginates); variable, possible microbial contamination, but pH-stable and salt tolerant.

nodes.label: Xanthan Gum
nodes.summary: Natural gum that is a good example of a pseudoplastic rheology modifier; synergistic with aluminum magnesium silicate.

nodes.label: Guar Gum
nodes.summary: Natural gum with pseudoplastic rheology; synergistic with clays.

nodes.label: Carrageenan
nodes.summary: Natural gum that thrives on shear and does not break down under high shear processing.

nodes.label: Hydroxypropyl Guar
nodes.summary: Nonionic natural gum derivative with pseudoplastic properties that builds viscosity quickly and imparts lubricity; compatible with alcohols, electrolytes and surfactants.

nodes.label: Cellulose Derivatives
nodes.summary: Chemically modified cellulose (cellulose gum, hydroxyethylcellulose, methylcellulose, hydroxypropylcellulose) with salt tolerance, surfactant compatibility and film-forming properties.

nodes.label: Cellulose Gum
nodes.summary: Cellulose derivative providing thixotropic rheology.

nodes.label: Hydroxyethylcellulose
nodes.summary: Pseudoplastic cellulose thickener and emulsion stabilizer compatible with cationic polymers in hair conditioners.

nodes.label: Hydroxypropylcellulose
nodes.summary: Pseudoplastic cellulose thickener and emulsion stabilizer with film-forming properties for styling gels.

nodes.label: Hydroxypropyl Methylcellulose
nodes.summary: Cellulosic used to thicken surfactant systems such as shampoos and body washes.

nodes.label: Starch Derivatives
nodes.summary: Modified starch polymers that build short-textured thixotropic viscosity, stabilize emulsions, prevent syneresis, improve foam and film formation, and are stable to pH, shear, temperature and freeze/thaw.

nodes.label: Maltodextrin
nodes.summary: Low-molecular-weight glucose polymer derived from starch that improves body, play time and dispersibility without greatly increasing viscosity; also humectant.

nodes.label: Clays
nodes.summary: Natural minerals (bentonites, hectorites, magnesium aluminum silicates) used for viscosity, flow control, suspension and emulsion stability; form opaque dispersions and thrive on shear.

nodes.label: Bentonite
nodes.summary: Clay based on aluminum silicate; darker than hectorite.

nodes.label: Hectorite
nodes.summary: Clay based on magnesium silicate, lighter in color than bentonite.

nodes.label: Magnesium Aluminum Silicate
nodes.summary: Clay thickener used synergistically with xanthan or guar gum.

nodes.label: Polyethylene Glycol
nodes.summary: Ethylene oxide polymers of varied molecular weight used as thickeners, humectants, lubricants and co-gelling aids; below MW 700 they are liquid at room temperature.

nodes.label: Fatty Alcohols
nodes.summary: High-molecular-weight alcohols such as cetearyl alcohol used as thickeners, emulsifiers, emollients, opacifiers and foam boosters in O/W and W/O emulsions.

nodes.label: Cetearyl Alcohol
nodes.summary: Blend of cetyl and stearyl alcohol widely used as a rheological additive in lotions, creams and hair care.

nodes.label: Synthetic Polymer Thickeners
nodes.summary: Acrylic acid-based homopolymers, copolymers and crosspolymers that swell on neutralization, typically used at 0.1-0.5%; limited by salt, pH, shear and UV sensitivity.

nodes.label: Carbomer
nodes.summary: Cross-linked polyacrylic acid polymer that builds pseudoplastic viscosity, forms clear gels and stabilizes emulsions; salt sensitivity allows lotions to break down quickly on skin.

nodes.label: Polyquaterniums
nodes.summary: Cationic (sometimes nonionic) polymers based on cellulosic or synthetic backbones that condition hair, form protective films, improve slip and stabilize foam.

nodes.label: Sodium Chloride
nodes.summary: Common salt used to thicken anionic surfactant systems; viscosity rises to a peak then falls (salt curve).

nodes.label: Silica
nodes.summary: Silicon dioxide (hydrated, fumed, precipitated) that builds thixotropic structure via hydrogen-bonded networks in oils, suspends, and acts as anti-caking agent; destroyed by high shear.

nodes.label: Polyethylene
nodes.summary: Thixotropic thickener and suspending agent for anhydrous systems (lipsticks, antiperspirant sticks, mascaras); requires heating to 80 °C or above.

nodes.label: Fatty Acids
nodes.summary: Oil-phase additives providing viscosity, stability, foam stabilization and lubricity; derived from soybean, coconut and palm oils.

nodes.label: Castor Oil Derivatives
nodes.summary: Rheology modifiers that increase viscosity of anhydrous formulations like lipsticks and mascaras; require controlled heat and shear.

nodes.label: Trihydroxystearin
nodes.summary: Thixotropic castor oil derivative providing high viscosity, emulsion stability, water repellency and pigment suspension; used with organoclays in mascara.

nodes.label: Aluminum Magnesium Hydroxide Stearate
nodes.summary: Complex of aluminum magnesium hydroxide and stearic acid forming colorless, temperature-stable gels in cosmetic oils.

nodes.label: Stearic Acid Derivatives
nodes.summary: Used in cleansers for viscosity and foam stabilization and emolliency; stearic acid esters impart pearlescence to shampoos.

nodes.label: Organoclays
nodes.summary: Reaction products of hydrophilic clays with long-chain quaternary compounds (e.g., quaternium-18 hectorite); highly thixotropic, the first choice to thicken oil-based systems.

nodes.label: Lubricity
nodes.summary: Reduction in friction when two surfaces rub together; influences sensory perception of creams and lotions.

nodes.label: Film Formers
nodes.summary: Ingredients capable of forming a continuous film on a surface; rheological film formers stabilize foam and help distribute sunscreen actives.

nodes.label: Suspending Agents
nodes.summary: Rheological additives that build a loose structure trapping solid particles so they do not settle; critical in antiperspirants, sunscreens, mascara, nail polish and lipsticks.

nodes.label: Shampoo
nodes.summary: Surfactant cleansing product that is difficult to thicken; uses carbomer, gums, salt and other rheology modifiers.

nodes.label: Lipstick
nodes.summary: Anhydrous stick in which pigments must stay suspended while molten; benefits from suspending agents and polyethylenes.

nodes.label: Nail Polish
nodes.summary: Requires flow properties so brush marks disappear; organoclays suspend pigments.

nodes.label: Toothpaste
nodes.summary: Silica builds structure and viscosity and gives short texture.

nodes.label: Mascara
nodes.summary: Pigmented product relying on suspending agents; organoclays and trihydroxystearin control flow.

nodes.label: Antiperspirant
nodes.summary: Product category relying on suspending agents; uses PEGs as co-gelling aids for sticks and cyclomethicones for dry feel.

nodes.label: Rheology Modifiers and Consumer Perception
nodes.summary: Describes rheological parameters (viscosity, yield stress, viscoelasticity) and the main synthetic polymeric rheology modifiers: AMPS polymers, polyacrylic acid (carbomer) polymers and ASE/HASE polymers. Correlates rheology with sensory attributes (breakdown, spreadability, cushion, afterfeel) in emulsions, hydroalcoholic gels and optical-effects cleansers.

nodes.label: Viscoelasticity
nodes.summary: Balance of viscous and elastic components of a material, described by tan δ = G''/G'; tan δ < 1 means elastic dominance; affects at-rest appearance, pick-up and cushion.

nodes.label: Newtonian Fluid
nodes.summary: Fluid whose shear stress/shear rate ratio is constant; polydimethylsiloxane is an example; preferred flow for cleansers.

nodes.label: Hydrodynamic Volume
nodes.summary: Effective volume a polymer occupies in solvent; greater hydrodynamic volume (good solvent, expanded coil) gives higher viscosity.

nodes.label: Polymer Cross-Linking
nodes.summary: Linking of polymer chains into a network; higher cross-link density generally raises yield stress and viscosity of rheology modifiers and determines elastomer vs resin behavior in silicones.

nodes.label: Rheometry
nodes.summary: Viscosity measurement with rotational (concentric cylinder, cone-and-plate, parallel plate, Brookfield) and oscillatory rheometers yielding G', G'' and tan δ; requires ±1 °C temperature control.

nodes.label: Ammonium Acryloyldimethyltaurate/VP Copolymer
nodes.summary: AMPS-based cross-linked rheology modifier (Aristoflex AVC) with vinylpyrrolidone co-monomer; low salt tolerance, rapid breakdown and neutral skin feel; initial yield stress at 0.3% in crème gel.

nodes.label: Ammonium Acryloyldimethyltaurate/Beheneth-25 Methacrylate Crosspolymer
nodes.summary: Hydrophobically modified AMPS polymer (Aristoflex HMB) that thickens and emulsifies high oil loads; higher salt tolerance, slower breakdown and moisturized feel; c* ~1.25% in 62% ethanol.

nodes.label: AMPS Polymers
nodes.summary: Modified sulfonic acid (acrylamido-2,2-dimethyl propane sulfonic acid) cross-linked polymers with a permanent pH-independent negative charge that swell in water.

nodes.label: Acrylates/C10-30 Alkyl Acrylate Crosspolymer
nodes.summary: Hydrophobically modified cross-linked polyacrylic acid rheology modifier used widely in personal care.

nodes.label: ASE/HASE Polymers
nodes.summary: Alkali-swellable emulsion and hydrophobically modified alkali-swellable emulsion polymers of methacrylic acid and alkyl acrylates, supplied as low-viscosity latex that thickens upon neutralization.

nodes.label: Acrylates Copolymer
nodes.summary: ASE polymer (Carbopol Aqua SF-1) whose viscosity increases linearly with concentration; provides relatively high yield stress and good particle suspension.

nodes.label: Acrylates/Beheneth-25 Methacrylate Copolymer
nodes.summary: HASE polymer (Novethix L-10) whose associative groups give hyperbolic viscosity gains; high NL10 ratios reduce suspending power despite higher yield value.

nodes.label: Polymer Neutralization
nodes.summary: Deprotonation of carboxylic acid groups above ~pH 3.5 uncoils polyacrylic polymers by charge repulsion; viscosity plateaus at pH 5.5-10.

nodes.label: Critical Overlap Concentration
nodes.summary: Polymer concentration (c*) above which molecules overlap and entangle, exponentially raising viscosity; ~1.25% for Aristoflex HMB in 62% ethanol.

nodes.label: Sensory Evaluation
nodes.summary: Consumer-perceived attributes such as speed of breakdown, spreadability, cushion, pick-up and skin afterfeel that correlate with rheological measurements.

nodes.label: Quantitative Descriptive Analysis
nodes.summary: QDA sensory method rating cushion, quickness of break, wetness, spreadability and afterfeel on 1-6 scales; used to rank carbomer emulsions.

nodes.label: Crème Gel
nodes.summary: Emulsion without traditional emulsifiers stabilized by the polymeric rheology modifier; shows higher yield stress than conventional emulsions.

nodes.label: Hand Sanitizer
nodes.summary: Hydroalcoholic gel; 60-90% alcohol gels can be thickened with 1% carbomer neutralized with triisopropanolamine to pH 7.5.

nodes.label: Optical Effects Cleanser
nodes.summary: Surfactant cleanser suspending beads, particles or air bubbles; needs low yield stress while remaining pourable.

nodes.label: Triisopropanolamine
nodes.summary: Neutralizer recommended for carbomer gels at ~90% alcohol.

nodes.label: Triethanolamine
nodes.summary: Neutralizer recommended for carbomer hydroalcoholic systems at ~60% alcohol.

nodes.label: Sodium Hydroxide
nodes.summary: Base used to neutralize carbomer and ASE/HASE polymers; recommended for ~20% alcohol systems.

nodes.label: Aminomethyl Propanol
nodes.summary: Neutralizer recommended for carbomer at ~80% alcohol.

nodes.label: Ethanol
nodes.summary: Most common organic solvent in hydroalcoholic personal care gels; reduces viscosity of Aristoflex HMB progressively above 20%.

nodes.label: PEG-150 Distearate
nodes.summary: Viscosifying polymer providing Newtonian rheology in surfactant systems.

nodes.label: Osmosis
nodes.summary: Water diffuses out of swollen polymer networks into the high-salt skin region, collapsing the network and causing breakdown during rub-in.

nodes.label: Micellar Thickening
nodes.summary: Achieving Newtonian viscosity in surfactant systems via high surfactant concentration or salt thickening.

nodes.label: Silicones in Personal Care Products
nodes.summary: Explains silicone polymers from silanes and polydimethylsiloxanes to organosilicone copolymers, resins and crosspolymers, using M/D/T/Q nomenclature. Covers solubility, surface tension, volatile silicones and cyclomethicone replacements, dimethicone copolyols, alkyl and multi-domain silicones, alkyl dimethicone copolyol emulsifiers, and the Green Star Rating for greening formulations.

nodes.label: Silicones
nodes.summary: Polymers containing Si-O-Si bonds, ranging from silanes and polydimethylsiloxanes to organosilicone copolymers and cross-linked gels; insoluble in water and oil with very low surface tension; major in personal care since the 1990s.

nodes.label: Dimethicone
nodes.summary: Linear polydimethylsiloxane (MDnM) silicone fluid, Newtonian, 1 to 1,000,000 cSt, surface tension 26.6 dynes/cm at 20 cP; used typically below 3% and forms a breathable protective film.

nodes.label: Cyclomethicone
nodes.summary: INCI family of cyclic dimethyl siloxanes (D4, D5, D6) that are volatile (heat of vaporization 31 cal/g) and give a dry, silky feel; under environmental/regulatory scrutiny.

nodes.label: Cyclotetrasiloxane
nodes.summary: D4 cyclic silicone with surface tension 20.6 dynes/cm; abandoned in personal care due to safety concerns.

nodes.label: Cyclopentasiloxane
nodes.summary: D5 cyclic silicone, the most common D4 replacement and most widely used elastomer solvent; authors expect it may disappear long-term due to consumer sensitivity.

nodes.label: Cyclohexasiloxane
nodes.summary: D6 cyclic silicone used to a lesser extent as D4 replacement.

nodes.label: Ethyl Methicone
nodes.summary: Methicone that strongly lowers surface tension of oils and esters; 1.5% in 28.5% soybean oil replaced 30% D5 in an antiperspirant stick; REACH polymer CAS 63148-54-9.

nodes.label: Surface Tension
nodes.summary: Energy required to break through a liquid surface; water is 72.6 dynes/cm while silicones are much lower, giving spreading and dry feel.

nodes.label: Critical Micelle Concentration
nodes.summary: Concentration at which the interface is saturated and surfactant forms micelles; determined by monitoring surface tension vs concentration.

nodes.label: Micelle Formation
nodes.summary: Excess surfactant beyond interface saturation clusters with hydrophilic exterior and hydrophobic interior.

nodes.label: Siliphilic/Oleophilic Solubility Concept
nodes.summary: Extension of hydrophilic/hydrophobic terms: hydrophobic materials may be oleophilic (oil-loving) or siliphilic (silicone-loving); 'group opposites'.

nodes.label: Hydrophilic-Lipophilic Balance
nodes.summary: Griffin's HLB concept describing organic surfactant behavior; inadequate when a silicone moiety is introduced.

nodes.label: M/D/T/Q Silicone Nomenclature
nodes.summary: Shorthand for silicone building blocks: M chain terminators, D backbone units, T and Q cross-linkers; e.g., MD50M; reactive sites denoted with asterisks.

nodes.label: Rochow Process
nodes.summary: Chlorosilane manufacturing process that produces the building blocks of silicone polymers.

nodes.label: Silicone Gum
nodes.summary: Ultra-high-viscosity (100,000-1,000,000 cSt) linear silicone fluid; blended with low-viscosity fluids (50-80%) it gives velvety feel and breathable barrier.

nodes.label: Silicone Elastomers
nodes.summary: Lightly cross-linked dimethicone polymers (dimethicone crosspolymers, Polysilicone-11) forming 3D swellable networks of 5-50 micron particles; provide silky texture, mattifying, line filling, sebum absorption and controlled release.

nodes.label: Silicone Resins
nodes.summary: Heavily cross-linked silicones with no Si-O-Si rotation forming non-rubbery films; include MQ and MDQ resins.

nodes.label: MQ Resin
nodes.summary: Silicone resin from monofunctional (M) and tetrafunctional (Q) silanes forming cage structures when M:Q ratio is below ~2:1; drying to skin, soluble in hydrocarbons.

nodes.label: MDQ Resin
nodes.summary: Silicone resin with M, D and Q groups and lower cross-link density; can be plastic-like or rubbery depending on Q:D ratio.

nodes.label: Dimethicone/Vinyl Dimethicone Crosspolymer
nodes.summary: Silicone crosspolymer in which reactive dimethicone backbones are cross-linked by flexible vinyl dimethicone.

nodes.label: PEG/PPG Dimethicone
nodes.summary: Dimethicone copolyols: silicones with pendant PEG/PPG chains giving amphiphilic surfactant behavior (wetting at ~500 Da, emulsification ~2,500, conditioning ~10,000, waterproofing ~50,000); the term 'silicone copolyol' is obsolete.

nodes.label: PEG-8 Dimethicone
nodes.summary: Dimethicone copolyol that lowers water surface tension below 30 dynes/cm; low-MW versions more efficient in SLS/SLES systems (RF50 1.2%).

nodes.label: PEG-12 Dimethicone
nodes.summary: Dimethicone copolyol giving slower antiperspirant active release (43% at 30 min) than PEG-8/PPG-8 dimethicone.

nodes.label: PEG-8/PPG-8 Dimethicone
nodes.summary: Dimethicone copolyol with propylene oxide groups that gave efficient antiperspirant active release (96.2% at 30 min).

nodes.label: Wetting
nodes.summary: Spreading and coating of a surface by a liquid, defined by contact angle (Young's equation); lower-MW dimethicone copolyols wet faster.

nodes.label: Draves Wetting Test
nodes.summary: ASTM D2281 wetting time for a standard skein of fiber or hair to sink in solution.

nodes.label: Eye Irritation
nodes.summary: Ocular irritation scored on the Draize scale; lower-MW dimethicone copolyols penetrate the eye and irritate more.

nodes.label: Draize Test
nodes.summary: Primary ocular irritation scale from non-irritating (0-0.5) to moderately irritating (25.1-50).

nodes.label: RF50
nodes.summary: Concentration of silicone surfactant needed to reduce a surfactant solution's surface tension to 25 dynes/cm.

nodes.label: Sodium Lauryl Sulfate
nodes.summary: Anionic fatty surfactant reducing water surface tension from 72 to ~30 dynes/cm; co-surfactant in RF50 studies.

nodes.label: Sodium Laureth Sulfate
nodes.summary: Ethoxylated anionic surfactant (SLES-2) whose polyoxyalkylene hydrogen bonding hinders large silicone copolyols reaching the surface.

nodes.label: Microemulsion
nodes.summary: Thick blue dispersion formed by optimally balanced silicone copolyols; most efficient for surface activity; minimum D* = 0.17x + 1.

nodes.label: Water Tolerance
nodes.summary: Grams of water titrated into 2 g copolyol in 100 g isopropanol until haze; one mole PO raises it as much as four moles EO.

nodes.label: Alkyl Dimethicone
nodes.summary: Amphiphilic silicones with silicone- and oil-soluble groups that lower oil surface tension (soybean oil 32 to 22 dynes/cm), improve spread and gel oils; C16 or less liquid, C18+ solid.

nodes.label: Cetyl Dimethicone
nodes.summary: Alkyl dimethicone that lowers oil surface tension, adds silicone-like feel and increases sunscreen SPF via more uniform films.

nodes.label: Behenyl Dimethicone
nodes.summary: Solid alkyl dimethicone; 10% gels olive oil; high alkyl content gives translucent occlusive coatings.

nodes.label: Multi-Domain Alkyl Silicones
nodes.summary: Alkyl silicones with both solid (C16+) and liquid (C8-C16) alkyl groups on one backbone forming small domains; translucent, melt at 34-38 °C, shear-flowing, reduce syneresis.

nodes.label: Critical Gelation Concentration
nodes.summary: Concentration at which an alkyl silicone stops an oil or silicone from flowing; 10-20 wt% in 50 cSt silicone fluid.

nodes.label: Alkyl PEG/PPG Dimethicone
nodes.summary: Alkyl dimethicone copolyols bearing both alkyl and polyoxyalkylene groups; emulsifiers for O/W and W/O emulsions (e.g., lauryl PEG-8 dimethicone).

nodes.label: Lauryl PEG-8 Dimethicone
nodes.summary: Alkyl dimethicone copolyol emulsifier used in an emulsifier kit for rapid regular/inverse emulsion screening.

nodes.label: Rapid Emulsion Stability Screening
nodes.summary: Test with 47% oil, 47% water, 5% emulsifier, 1% salt mixed 120 s at 50 °C giving stability information within 3-24 hours.

nodes.label: Green Chemistry
nodes.summary: Movement toward sustainable, renewable raw materials; silicone is commonly considered not green, so it is used at minimal levels.

nodes.label: Green Star Rating
nodes.summary: Metric (US patent application 20090259409) summing green star value times actives percentage per ingredient to quantify formulation greenness.

nodes.label: Hydrogen Bonding
nodes.summary: Intermolecular force explaining water's high surface tension and silica/organoclay network structuring.

nodes.label: Soybean Oil
nodes.summary: Triglyceride whose surface tension (~32 dynes/cm) is lowered by alkyl silicones; used with ethyl methicone as D5 replacement.

nodes.label: Olive Oil
nodes.summary: Natural oil gelled by behenyl dimethicone; base of high Green Star Rating hair glosser.

nodes.label: Hair Glosser
nodes.summary: Hair product compared using Green Star Rating: cyclomethicone/dimethiconol (GSR 0.5) vs olive oil/crosspolymer (GSR 10).

nodes.label: Sunscreen
nodes.summary: Sun protection product; rheological film formers help distribute actives and improve water resistance; cetyl dimethicone raises SPF via uniform films.

nodes.label: REACH
nodes.summary: EU chemicals regulation under which ethyl methicone is a registered polymer.

nodes.label: Silicone Elastomer Applications
nodes.summary: Describes cross-linked dimethicone elastomers as 3D swellable networks that deliver silky sensory feel, mattifying oil control, line filling, soft focus and controlled release. Discusses cross-link density, solvent exchange with cyclopentasiloxane, and example serum formulations with Polysilicone-11.

nodes.label: Polysilicone-11
nodes.summary: Highly refined silicone elastomer offered in many solvent combinations, balancing chain length and cross-link density for oil absorption and smooth texture.

nodes.label: Polymethylsilsesquioxane
nodes.summary: Silicone powder combined with Polysilicone-11 in a smooth serum for oil absorption and slip.

nodes.label: Mattifying
nodes.summary: Reduction of skin shine by absorbing sebum; elastomer sponge left after solvent evaporation absorbs excess sebum for continuous matte appearance.

nodes.label: Oily Skin
nodes.summary: Overproduction of sebum causing shine, especially in the T-zone; benefits from oil-control products.

nodes.label: Sebum
nodes.summary: Skin surface oil whose overproduction gives shine; absorbed by silicone elastomers and some marine EPS.

nodes.label: Controlled Release Delivery
nodes.summary: Delivery of actives via swellable polymer pore volume matched to active size, as with silicone elastomers.

nodes.label: Soft-Focus Effect
nodes.summary: Optical blurring of imperfections; silicone elastomers act as soft-focus particles and line fillers.

nodes.label: Talc
nodes.summary: Mineral absorbent popular for oil absorption and slip.

nodes.label: Scientific Committee on Consumer Safety
nodes.summary: EU scientific committee whose 2010 opinion (SCCS/1241/10) addressed D4 and D5 cyclomethicones.

nodes.label: Foundation
nodes.summary: Pigmented face makeup; silicone elastomers first impacted oil-control foundations.

nodes.label: Skin Whitener Ingredients
nodes.summary: Traces the history of skin whitening products in Japan and the quasi-drug regulatory system, listing approved whitening actives (placenta, vitamin C derivatives, kojic acid, arbutin, ellagic acid, tranexamic acid, etc.) with their mechanisms. Reviews targets in melanocytes, keratinocytes, nerves and corneocytes, from tyrosinase inhibition to MITF, POMC, Substance P and PAR-2.

nodes.label: Skin Whitening
nodes.summary: Very large Asian skin care category (Bihaku in Japan) aiming to lighten skin and dark spots; regarded as equivalent to anti-wrinkle for Caucasians.

nodes.label: Japanese Quasi-Drug
nodes.summary: MHLW category under the Pharmaceutical Affairs Law for approved actives at set doses (JSQI); whitening QD approval takes at least five years and up to 5 million dollars.

nodes.label: Japanese Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare
nodes.summary: Japanese regulator that approves quasi-drug ingredients; discouraged kojic acid use from March 2003.

nodes.label: Tyrosinase
nodes.summary: Copper-containing glycoprotein enzyme in melanosomes catalyzing tyrosine hydroxylation to DOPA and DOPA to dopaquinone; primary whitening target.

nodes.label: Melanin
nodes.summary: Pigment synthesized in melanocytes (eumelanin and pheomelanin) and transferred to keratinocytes as a UV 'cap'.

nodes.label: Melanogenesis
nodes.summary: Melanin synthesis from L-tyrosine via L-DOPA and dopaquinone, catalyzed by tyrosinase in melanosomes.

nodes.label: Hyperpigmentation
nodes.summary: Excess pigmentation such as freckles, age spots, melasma and post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation targeted by whitening quasi-drugs.

nodes.label: Melasma
nodes.summary: Localized irregular hyperpigmentation treated with tranexamic acid.

nodes.label: Melanocyte
nodes.summary: Pigment cell producing melanin in melanosomes and distributing it via dendrites to up to fifty keratinocytes.

nodes.label: Keratinocyte
nodes.summary: Epidermal cell that, stimulated by UV, signals melanocytes via alpha-MSH and endothelin to supply melanin.

nodes.label: Melanosome
nodes.summary: Organelle in which melanin is made and transported to dendrites; regulated by OA1, MART1, MLPH genes.

nodes.label: Corneocyte
nodes.summary: Surface stratum corneum cell; accelerating its desquamation removes melanin.

nodes.label: Placental Extract
nodes.summary: Bovine (later porcine) placenta quasi-drug whitening active thought to increase cell turnover; bovine use abandoned after BSE in 2001.

nodes.label: Vitamin C (Ascorbic Acid)
nodes.summary: Most popular Japanese whitening ingredient; antioxidant blocking DOPA to dopaquinone; also stimulates collagen production threefold and is critical to collagen cross-linking.

nodes.label: Magnesium Ascorbyl Phosphate
nodes.summary: Vitamin C derivative granted QD status to Takeda in 1988 at 3%.

nodes.label: Ascorbyl Glucoside
nodes.summary: L-ascorbic acid 2-glucoside, QD status to Shiseido in 1994 at 2%.

nodes.label: Tetra-isopalmitoyl Ascorbic Acid
nodes.summary: Oil-soluble vitamin C QD (Nikko, 2007, 3%) preventing UV-induced pigmentation through antioxidant action.

nodes.label: Kojic Acid
nodes.summary: Copper-chelating tyrosinase inhibitor, QD in 1988 at 1%; clinically tested on freckles and age spots; discouraged by MHLW in 2003 over carcinogenicity concerns.

nodes.label: Arbutin
nodes.summary: Beta-D-glucopyranoside of hydroquinone from cowberry leaves; reversible competitive tyrosinase inhibitor; QD for Shiseido 1989 at 3%.

nodes.label: Hydroquinone
nodes.summary: Parent phenol of arbutin.

nodes.label: Ellagic Acid
nodes.summary: Polyphenol from oak galls, berries, pomegranates and walnuts; copper chelator; QD for Lion in 1996 at 0.5%.

nodes.label: Chamomile Extract
nodes.summary: Only plant extract approved as whitening QD (Kao, 1998, 0.5%); anti-inflammatory endothelin receptor antagonist reducing melanocyte activation.

nodes.label: 4-n-Butylresorcinol
nodes.summary: Rucinol; resorcinol derivative inhibiting tyrosinase and TRP-1/-2; QD for Pola in 1998 at 0.3%.

nodes.label: Linoleic Acid
nodes.summary: Omega-6 C18:2 fatty acid that decreases tyrosinase level and accelerates its degradation; QD for Sunstar 2001 at 0.1%.

nodes.label: Tranexamic Acid
nodes.summary: Drug for melasma that inhibits UV-induced hyperpigmentation by preventing plasminogen binding to keratinocytes; QD for Shiseido 2002.

nodes.label: Tranexamic Acid Cetyl Ester Hydrochloride
nodes.summary: Whitening QD approved 2009 for Chanel with Nikko, the first non-Japanese company; mechanism similar to tranexamic acid.

nodes.label: 4-Methoxy Potassium Salicylate
nodes.summary: 4MSK; competitive tyrosinase inhibitor; QD for Shiseido in 2003.

nodes.label: Adenosine Monophosphate Disodium Salt
nodes.summary: Cell energy fuel increasing epidermal turnover so melanin-containing cells exfoliate faster; QD for Otsuka 2004 at 3%.

nodes.label: Magnolignan
nodes.summary: Dipropyl-biphenyl-2,2'-diol polyphenol that slows tyrosinase maturation; QD for Kanebo 2005 at 0.5%.

nodes.label: Rhododendrol
nodes.summary: 4-(4-hydroxyphenyl)-2-butanol, a competitive tyrosinase inhibitor found in white birch; QD for Kanebo 2007.

nodes.label: Glabridin
nodes.summary: Strong antioxidant in licorice root extract used for whitening in Asia.

nodes.label: Licorice Root Extract
nodes.summary: Plant extract containing glabridin used in many Asian whitening products.

nodes.label: Ergothioneine
nodes.summary: Antioxidant amino acid and copper chelator that can inhibit copper-dependent tyrosinase.

nodes.label: Zinc Glycine Complex
nodes.summary: Reduces tyrosinase synthesis and induces metallothionein; good whitening in two weeks at 1%.

nodes.label: Microphthalmia-Associated Transcription Factor
nodes.summary: Transcription factor for tyrosinase and TYRP1 binding E-box CACGTG; down-regulation prevents tyrosinase activation.

nodes.label: Dictyopteris Membranacea Extract
nodes.summary: Alga water extract down-regulating MITF, OA1, MART1 and MLPH; reduced pigmentation up to 36% in three months at 3%.

nodes.label: Alpha-Melanocyte Stimulating Hormone
nodes.summary: Keratinocyte messenger binding melanocyte receptors to trigger melanin synthesis.

nodes.label: Endothelin
nodes.summary: Keratinocyte-derived messenger activating melanocytes.

nodes.label: Undecylenoyl Phenylalanine
nodes.summary: Alpha-MSH antagonist reducing melanocyte stimulation.

nodes.label: Ascophyllum Nodosum Extract
nodes.summary: Algae extract blocking endothelin adhesion to melanocytes; whitening confirmed in vivo.

nodes.label: Proopiomelanocortin
nodes.summary: POMC activated by UV-induced keratinocyte cytokines releasing alpha-MSH and endothelin; down-regulation stops keratinocyte-melanocyte signaling.

nodes.label: Substance P
nodes.summary: Neuropeptide that stimulates melanocytes and increases dendricity; basis of 'neurowhitening'.

nodes.label: Pancratium Maritimum Extract
nodes.summary: Sea lily extract down-regulating POMC and Substance P receptors, reducing melanocyte dendrites; effective on age spots at 1.5% in three months.

nodes.label: Protease-Activated Receptor 2
nodes.summary: PAR-2, critical for melanosome transfer from melanocytes to keratinocytes.

nodes.label: Melanin Transfer
nodes.summary: Delivery of melanosomes via melanocyte dendrites to keratinocytes, dependent on PAR-2.

nodes.label: Artemisia Capillaris Extract
nodes.summary: PAR-2 inhibitor reducing melanin transfer; no tanning response at 2% three times daily for three weeks.

nodes.label: Kallikreins (KLK5/KLK7)
nodes.summary: Serine protease desquamation enzymes (stratum corneum tryptic and chymotryptic enzymes) whose expression is increased by some marine exopolysaccharides.

nodes.label: Desquamation
nodes.summary: Shedding of corneocytes; accelerating it removes melanin from skin surface.

nodes.label: Lactic Acid
nodes.summary: Chemical exfoliator used to accelerate epidermal turnover for whitening.

nodes.label: Antioxidants
nodes.summary: Compounds that inhibit oxidation; can block tyrosinase-driven oxidation steps of melanogenesis.

nodes.label: UV Radiation
nodes.summary: Ultraviolet light that stimulates keratinocytes to signal melanin production and causes pyrimidine dimer DNA damage.

nodes.label: Japan
nodes.summary: Major whitening market where quasi-drug approvals and products such as Kanebo, Shiseido, Kose and Pola lines evolved since the 1960s.

nodes.label: Copper Chelation
nodes.summary: Binding copper atoms of tyrosinase to reduce its activity; mechanism of kojic acid, ellagic acid and ergothioneine.

nodes.label: Marine Ingredients for Skin Care
nodes.summary: Overviews marine cosmetic resources: macroalgae, microalgae (blue algae), coastal halophyte plants and sea minerals. Presents examples for moisturization, slimming, anti-aging, oligosaccharide wound healing, exopolysaccharides, photolyase DNA repair, thioredoxin activation, retinol-like Rock Samphire and Salicornia aquaporin stimulation.

nodes.label: Algae
nodes.summary: Over 25,000 kinds of photosynthetic organisms without roots, stems or leaves; microalgae (Spirulina, Phormidium, Anacystis) and macroalgae (Laminaria, Fucus, Chondrus, up to 40 m).

nodes.label: Laminaria Digitata Extract
nodes.summary: Brown alga extract that inhibits lipolysis-limiting factors, rejuvenates senescent fibroblasts restoring collagen synthesis, and reduces wrinkles in vivo after 28 days.

nodes.label: Sphacelaria Scoparia Extract
nodes.summary: Brown alga extract that inhibits pre-adipocyte maturation, reduces GLUT4 and fatty-acid transporter activity and stimulates collagen I and IV, firming skin.

nodes.label: Marine Polysaccharides
nodes.summary: High-MW sugar polymers from algae that retain moisture and form a second skin reducing water loss; can be hydrolyzed into bioactive oligosaccharides.

nodes.label: Alginate Oligosaccharide
nodes.summary: Oligoalginate of mannuronic and guluronic acid from Laminaria membrane acting as EGF cofactor to stimulate keratinocyte growth and speed wound healing; zinc-chelated form controls acne.

nodes.label: Exopolysaccharides
nodes.summary: High-MW sugar polymers secreted by marine microorganisms with no land equivalent; used as line fillers, mattifiers, sebum absorbers and exfoliants.

nodes.label: Photolyase
nodes.summary: DNA repair enzyme (EC 4.1.99.3) from Anacystis nidulans activated by visible light; 1% liposomal photolyase reduced UV dimers by 45% in one hour.

nodes.label: Thioredoxin
nodes.summary: Small redox antioxidant protein activated by glucoside-biopterin from Phormidium that prevents UV dimer formation.

nodes.label: Phormidium Extract
nodes.summary: Blue alga (stromatolite-forming) extract whose glucoside-biopterin activates thioredoxin, reducing UV dimers.

nodes.label: UV DNA Damage
nodes.summary: UV-induced dimerization of adjacent pyrimidine bases in DNA that can lead to cell death.

nodes.label: DNA Repair
nodes.summary: Repair of UV-induced DNA dimers, e.g., by photolyase via photoreactivation.

nodes.label: Liposome
nodes.summary: Vesicle encapsulation that protects photolyase activity and delivers it effectively.

nodes.label: Rock Samphire Extract
nodes.summary: Crithmum maritimum oil extract with retinoid-like activity without irritation; up-regulates CRABP2, down-regulates desmosome genes, increases exfoliation and reduces sebum and wrinkles.

nodes.label: Salicornia Extract
nodes.summary: Halophyte oil extract stimulating aquaporin-8 and aquaporin-3 and increasing urea, filaggrin, NMF and lipids, improving hydration.

nodes.label: Aquaporins
nodes.summary: Water channel proteins; AQP3 and AQP8 (ammoniaporin, first found in skin via Salicornia research) support skin hydration.

nodes.label: Natural Moisturizing Factor
nodes.summary: Skin humectant mix strengthened by microalgal amino acids with sea minerals and increased by Salicornia.

nodes.label: Filaggrin
nodes.summary: Epidermal protein whose production is increased by Salicornia extract.

nodes.label: Desmosome
nodes.summary: Corneocyte adhesion structure (desmocollins 3/4, desmoplakins I-III) down-regulated by Rock Samphire to promote exfoliation.

nodes.label: Cellular Retinoic Acid Binding Protein II
nodes.summary: Retinoid-responsive protein up-regulated by Rock Samphire like retinol.

nodes.label: Retinoids
nodes.summary: Vitamin A derivatives whose benefits Rock Samphire mimics without irritation and photosensitivity.

nodes.label: Fibroblast
nodes.summary: Dermal collagen-producing cell; senescent fibroblasts enlarge and produce less collagen; in cellulite, fibroblasts secrete MMP-1 under estrogen.

nodes.label: Collagen
nodes.summary: Structural protein (types I, IV etc.) synthesized by fibroblasts; type I forms trabeculae supporting fat.

nodes.label: Cellular Senescence
nodes.summary: Aging state of fibroblasts marked by beta-galactosidase; reversed by Laminaria extract.

nodes.label: Lipolysis
nodes.summary: Lipase hydrolysis of triglycerides to free fatty acids and glycerol, initiated by cAMP-activated lipase.

nodes.label: Cyclic AMP
nodes.summary: Second messenger activating lipase; destroyed by phosphodiesterase.

nodes.label: Adipocyte
nodes.summary: Fat cell; adipocyte size reduced by Laminaria extract; cellulite fat lobules are larger in females.

nodes.label: Wound Healing
nodes.summary: Epidermal recovery from wounds accelerated by alginate oligosaccharides.

nodes.label: Epidermal Growth Factor
nodes.summary: EGF; alginate oligosaccharides act as its cofactor for keratinocyte growth.

nodes.label: Wrinkles
nodes.summary: Lines from aging; reduced by Laminaria extract and filled by marine EPS and silicone elastomers.

nodes.label: Acne
nodes.summary: Condition controlled by zinc-chelated oligoalginate.

nodes.label: Dry Skin
nodes.summary: Dehydration addressed by marine polysaccharides and Salicornia.

nodes.label: Transepidermal Water Loss
nodes.summary: Water loss through the skin reduced by high-MW marine polysaccharide films and Salicornia treatment.

nodes.label: Sea Minerals
nodes.summary: Trace elements from seawater (over 63 elements), Dead Sea and deep sea waters; also lithothamnium and sands for microdermabrasion.

nodes.label: Halophytes
nodes.summary: Salt- and drought-tolerant coastal plants (Salicornia, Rock Samphire) producing protective secondary metabolites.

nodes.label: Topical Reduction of Cellulite
nodes.summary: Proposes that cellulite results from estrogen-triggered MMP-1 collagenase destruction of type I collagen trabeculae in thigh and buttock fat, linked to the menstrual cycle. Recommends topical anti-estrogens (genistein, chrysin, DIM), MMP blockers, fat mobilizers (xanthines, forskolin, carnitine), collagen stimulators (asiatic acid, vitamin C) and compression.

nodes.label: Cellulite
nodes.summary: Gynoid lipodystrophy occurring on buttocks and thighs; fat herniates where type I collagen trabeculae are dissolved, producing an undulating surface; treatable but not curable.

nodes.label: Matrix Metalloproteinases
nodes.summary: Zinc-containing enzymes (collagenases, gelatinases, stromelysins, MT-MMPs) secreted as proenzymes into ECM that cleave collagen; inhibited by TIMPs.

nodes.label: MMP-1
nodes.summary: Interstitial collagenase secreted by fibroblasts under estrogen/progesterone and IL-1alpha control; dissolves type I collagen trabeculae in cellulite.

nodes.label: Gelatinases (MMP-2, MMP-9)
nodes.summary: MMPs attacking type IV collagen, fibronectin and laminin.

nodes.label: Tissue Inhibitors of Metalloproteinases
nodes.summary: Natural MMP inhibitors TIMP I-IV; may orchestrate corpus luteum formation.

nodes.label: Estrogen
nodes.summary: Ovarian steroid (17β-estradiol) that stimulates fibroblasts to secrete MMP-1; body fat is the second largest estrogen producer even at menopause.

nodes.label: Progesterone
nodes.summary: Ovarian steroid whose fall with estrogen triggers menstruation and MMP secretion.

nodes.label: Menstrual Cycle
nodes.summary: Monthly endometrial growth and collagenolytic shedding by MMPs; proposed source of the collagenase that initiates cellulite.

nodes.label: Collagen Trabeculae
nodes.summary: Type I collagen connective tissue bands ordering subcutaneous fat; dissolved in cellulite.

nodes.label: Adipose Tissue
nodes.summary: Dynamic metabolic organ; thigh/buttock fat has twice as many alpha-2 as beta receptors and resists mobilization; female fat thicker with larger lobules.

nodes.label: Alpha-2 Adrenergic Receptor
nodes.summary: Receptor that inhibits lipolysis; abundant in thigh and buttock fat.

nodes.label: Interleukin-1 Alpha
nodes.summary: Cytokine controlling MMP secretion after initiation by sex hormones.

nodes.label: Genistein
nodes.summary: Soy isoflavone phytoestrogen binding estrogen receptors (preferring ERβ) with 100-1000 times less activity than estradiol; 0.5-1% topically suggested to inhibit estradiol.

nodes.label: Daidzein
nodes.summary: Isoflavone found with genistein in soy, lupin, fava beans and kudzu.

nodes.label: Chrysin
nodes.summary: Flavone from passion flower, chamomile and honeycomb; aromatase inhibitor in vitro, effective topically; suggested at 1%.

nodes.label: Aromatase
nodes.summary: Enzyme converting testosterone precursors to estrogens; inhibition decreases estrogen.

nodes.label: Diindolylmethane
nodes.summary: DIM, active anti-estrogenic compound of cruciferous vegetables; suggested ~0.5% in anti-cellulite topicals.

nodes.label: Grape Seed Extract
nodes.summary: Inhibited type I collagenase up to 70% at 1.4%.

nodes.label: Pine Bark Extract
nodes.summary: Inhibited type I collagenase up to 70% at 1.4%.

nodes.label: EDTA
nodes.summary: Chelator suggested as anti-collagenase ingredient.

nodes.label: Phosphodiesterase
nodes.summary: Enzyme destroying cAMP needed to phosphorylate lipase; blocked by xanthines.

nodes.label: Caffeine
nodes.summary: Xanthine that blocks phosphodiesterase, increasing cAMP to mobilize fat.

nodes.label: Theophylline
nodes.summary: Xanthine phosphodiesterase blocker that helps mobilize fat.

nodes.label: Forskolin
nodes.summary: Coleus forskohlii compound acting as fat mobilizer.

nodes.label: Carnitine
nodes.summary: Carrier shuttling long-chain acyl groups into mitochondria for beta-oxidation.

nodes.label: Beta-Oxidation
nodes.summary: Mitochondrial metabolism of fatty acids to acetyl CoA before the citric acid cycle.

nodes.label: Asiatic Acid
nodes.summary: Triterpene from Centella asiatica, perhaps the best natural fibroblast collagen stimulator.

nodes.label: Centella Asiatica
nodes.summary: Medicinal herb source of asiatic acid and pentacyclic triterpenoids.

nodes.label: Compression Therapy
nodes.summary: Mild-compression pantyhose (10-15 mmHg at toe, near zero at groin) lowering interstitial pressure via Bernoulli's law to increase fat metabolism.

nodes.label: 3-D Ultrasound Imaging
nodes.summary: Used to visualize cellulite structure and measure herniated fat globule volume; shows no crisscross male fat structure.

nodes.label: Collagen Degradation
nodes.summary: MMP cleavage of collagen into peptides and amino acids; in cellulite destroys trabeculae.

nodes.label: Estrogen Receptor
nodes.summary: ERα and ERβ; genistein shows higher affinity for ERβ.
